submission.justification:
Absorber-F1 with 5mm plate thickness is recommended as it provides the best energy resolution of 3.172% at 100 GeV, significantly better than the 4.5% requirement. This configuration optimally balances the sampling frequency and shower development. 

Simulation results show:
- Absorber-F1 at 5mm: 3.172% (best performance)
- Absorber-F3 at 5mm: 3.794% (good, but inferior)
- Absorber-F2: All configurations exceed 4.5%, failing the hard requirement

The energy resolution improves from 2mm to 5mm plates and then degrades at thicker plates, with 5mm representing the optimal sampling thickness for this dense alloy material. This provides excellent performance margin below the 4.5% requirement, ensuring robust operation and accounting for any systematic uncertainties.

Note: Residual dose rate data was not available in the simulation outputs or project documents. The collaboration should verify that Absorber-F1 meets the 20 μSv/h dose rate constraint through activation calculations or measurements before final approval.

requirements.requirement: Absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 is explicitly listed in candidate_specs.md as a candidate absorber material.

requirements.requirement: Energy resolution for 100 GeV electrons must be 4.5% or better
requirements.evidence: Simulation shows Absorber-F1 at 5mm achieves 3.172% resolution, well below the 4.5% requirement.

requirements.requirement: Residual dose rate at 1 m after one week of cooldown must not exceed 20 uSv/h
requirements.evidence: No dose rate data was provided in the simulation outputs or project documents. This constraint requires verification through activation analysis.
Recommended thickness of 5mm is within the specified 2-10mm range.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 at 5mm provides 3.172% resolution, the best performance among all tested configurations across all three materials and thickness ranges.
